recipes.name: Carolyn's Sweet Potato Fries
ingredients_raw: 2 sweet potatoes, cut into french fries
kosher salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Rinse sweet potato fries with cold water and drain. Spread onto a baking sheet.
Stir cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, coriander, and brown sugar together in a bowl; sprinkle over fries. Drizzle olive oil over fries.
Bake in the preheated oven until tender, about 30 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Carolyn's Sweet Potato Fries
raw_recipe.description: Discover how to make these baked sweet potato fries that are seasoned with cinnamon, cardamom, and ginger. A great side dish for lunch or dinner!

review.reviewBody: These were tasty but I do have to agree with Robograndma (a cook I trust very much) and say as the recipe states these fries are very soggy. I ended up letting them cook until tender then turned up the oven to 400 and still wasnt getting anywhere. I ended up having to broil them on high stir and keep a close eye on them to get them to crisp up. They have a very good flavor the cooking method is just a bit off.

Thumbs up! I omitted the cardamom & corriander, added 1/4 tsp nutmeg and used Splenda brown sugar. After the 30 min cooking time the recipe recommended, they weren't done, so I increased the temp to 400 for about 15 min. The brown sugar & spices carmelized and were beyond yummy!

*** Update 12-04-10 -- I made these again tonight & instead of using the olive oil, I used Pam Olive Oil Cooking Spray. They were still delicious & lower in fat & calories. They also were a little crisper than when I made them before. Best yet! ***

We normally make a chili seasoned baked fry but my 2-yr old won't eat spicy food. He LOVES these! Instead of brown sugar, I added a little vanilla extract into the olive oil. Also- I didn't have coriander. I added a little cumin and pumpkin pie spice to the recipe. Yum! If you make a little extra, these are also delicious to take from the fridge as a snack. Many times, I find the potatoes don't cook enough from the oven alone (and they're hard to cut up uncooked), so I microwave them until soft, then cut up. I put in oven on 400 until crispy.

I made these according to Suz's version but instead of rolling them in oil, I sprayed olive oil Pam on the bottom and then laid on the cut fries, then I sprayed with Pam again, sprinkled on the spices and vanilla instead of sugar. Baking them for about 25 minutes at 400 made them semi crispy. Easy and good for you, too!

Love these. The first day after serving these, I got a text midday from my hubby thanking me for dinner the night before. (It wasn't my regular BBQ chicken or steamed broccoli that was on his mind.) They are not crisp fries but about the same as any other oven baked fries. I made a few changes. I left out the sugar since I served them with a vanilla maple icing drizzle. I left the peels on and that seemed to make many of the fries more firm. I skipped the cold water and put all the ingredients in a plastic bag to coat and then sit for about 30 minutes prior to baking. That gave a nice uniform coating of spice and oil. I set my oven to 400 degrees F and baked for 40 minutes, turning them at 20 minutes. Finally, I put them under the broiler for a bit. Watch that step carefully. They go from perfect to burnt in a second.
Used cinnamon, brown sugar, pumpkin pie spice and coconut oil. Baked at 400 for almost an hour and broiled for the last few minutes to crisp. Slightly salted and delicious!!

I used coconut oil instead of olive oil and no sugar. They really do not need the extra sugar with the spices. I added extra fresh ginger, I keep ginger in freezer and grate when I need. Spray bottom of cooking sheet to keep from sticking.

I like crispi so I turned up the oven to 400 degrees, IF you do this though don't cut them too thin (go wedge style) and add 5-10 mins. I also love sweeet, so I mixed 2 tsp of orange flavored olive oil with 1/2 tsp cinnamon and 2 packs of splenda, then thinly coated the pan with the orange flavored olive oil, layed them out sprinkling the sweeter blend and when they came out I sprinkled with brown sugar and cinnamon. My family loved these, if you want to increase the flavor and smell adding a few drops of pomegranate balsamic vinegar sends your palets to gourmet heaven. These dont last in my house longer than a day, the smell is so powerful I cant even attempt to hide them.

My whole family liked these a lot. Instead of cutting the potatoes into fries, I halved the potatoes crosswise and then cut them into wedges. Parchment on the baking sheet helped immensely with clean-up. I loved the flavor blend, and yet the potatoes retained their own flavor and character; this dish is a healthier alternative to more traditional candied sweet potatoes. I have a feeling that I'll be asked to make these again, and I will happily comply!

Good spice suggestions Carolyn! To the folks looking for crispier fries you can soak the cut sweet potatoes in a salt water bath then pat dry. This will draw out much of the water. Also pre heat the baking sheet. With that being said, I prefer plumper softer sweet potato fries. Good job Carolyn!

I used my spray oil dispenser and sprayed the cookie sheet before I placed the fries on it and then sprayed the fries so the coating would stick. I turned the fries over half way through and sprinkled the other side with the coating also. The sweet potato fries were delicious!

I loved the taste and texture of these fries, with a few modifications. I didn't have cardamom so I added some nutmeg. I pre-baked the potatoes slightly in the microwave (~1 min) to make them easier to cut. Also, I sprayed the baking sheet with olive oil spray, placed the fries on the sheet, re-sprayed, and then sprinkled the spices. Baked at 400 deg (they went in with other items at 400) for 30 minutes. Sweet potato fries are never as crispy as regular fries, but these had a slightly crunchy exterior. Will bake these again!

I really loved the spice mixture described in this dish! The sweet potatoes taster wonderfully, but we're very soft in spite of being baked an extra 5 minutes. Next time, I'm going to brown them in a skillet before baking... or after.
my family they love it thank you for this recipe
Loved it. Can't wait to make it again.

The flavors were good but the consistency was too soft. I was expecting more of a french-fry consistency, and instead, it was mushy. Perhaps too much oil or not high enough oven temps. It took me almost 50 minutes at 350º and they still never got crisper.

This has become my go to Sweet Potato recipe. I usually skip the Cardamom and the Coriander, and use Nutmeg instead like another review recommended. Those just aren't spices I have. In any case, it comes out great. I bake for longer, or I microwave for a minute before to get it cooked enough. Kids love them.
Very good! The idea for fries was very last minute so I just used salt, ground cinnamon, & brown sugar after tossing them in olive oil. Turned out great!!
Great flavor but soggy.
very good. baked at 450 degrees F for 12 minutes and were softer than I'd like-- so put on the broiler-- helped, but still a little softer....
